chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Muhammad b. Isma'il b. Bazi' from Abdullah b. Uthman from al-Husayn b. Mihran from Ishaq b. Ghalib from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever is ill-mannered has tormented himself.

key_terms.خلق: Khuluq (character/disposition) - one's habitual moral nature and behavioral tendencies
key_terms.عذب نفسه: Tormented himself - self-inflicted suffering through one's own bad character

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the consequences of having bad character?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a direct link between bad character and self-harm. The Arabic word 'khuluq' refers to one's habitual disposition and moral character. The Imam teaches that ill-mannered behavior is not merely harmful to others but constitutes self-punishment -- the person with bad character suffers most from their own behavior through social isolation, inner turmoil, and spiritual degradation. This teaching aligns with the broader Islamic emphasis on akhlaq (ethics) as central to faith.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from Muhammad b. Isma`il b. Bazi` from `Abdullah b. `Uthman from al-Husayn b. Mehran from Ishaq b. Ghalib from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
Whoever is ill-mannered has tormented himself.
